reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) comes entirely from a study on TaNbVTi-based RHEAs, not HfMoTaTiZr. It shows Al2O3 addition leads to Al solid-solution and TiO precipitation strengthening in that system, but provides no data on whether the same phases form, or whether density is reduced and room/high-temperature performance is maintained, in the chemically distinct HfMoTaTiZr alloy. The key premise of transferability is therefore unsupported.
premises: Al2O3 addition to a refractory high-entropy alloy introduces Al and O into the matrix
Al goes into solid solution, providing solid-solution strengthening
O reacts with Ti to form TiO precipitates, providing precipitation strengthening
These mechanisms improve yield strength and specific strength without catastrophic loss of plasticity
The approach is transferable to the HfMoTaTiZr alloy system
